html:
The Akokisa were a band of the Atakapa people who lived around Galveston Bay and the lower Trinity and Sabine rivers in Texas, in today's Houston area. They were close relatives of the Atakapa-Ishak of south-western Louisiana.

They lived by fishing, gathering shellfish and hunting, moving between the coast and inland camps with the seasons. To the south-west lived the Karankawa. In the 1700s they traded with French merchants from Louisiana. To keep the French out, the Spanish built a presidio and the mission of Nuestra Señora de la Luz in their country on the lower Trinity in the 1750s, but it was abandoned in 1771. Disease and war reduced the Akokisa, and by about 1800 the survivors had merged with other Atakapa.
